b:
The days of Karthigai dawn with that song of Trisha's about coming with lamps in hand on this good day

Lamps are woven into human life. Beyond religion, beyond culture, the science bound up with them is full of feeling..

When humans discovered fire they must have been afraid of it.. Everything put into it would have burned. Touch it and it would have scorched.. Who wouldn't fear a fire that turns giant trees to mere ash in seconds?

But there was some courage in him… where could it have come from?? Ah, but that brave one was a woman.. While the man went out to hunt, she must have tried handling fire at home.. She is the mother of the chemistry called cooking.. Perhaps it is a bond she created.. to this day I cannot get my mother out of the kitchen.. her heart does not easily agree to give up her mother's dowry

He tamed that fire a little more.. and the lamp appeared.. It was not terrifying like a forest fire.. Its flame became a light.. It gave warmth and light up close.. The one who had seen only the sun and moon as sources of light now began to see fire as a god too. To this day, in many religions, languages and cultures, there is the custom of lighting lamps.

In our house there was never a custom of celebrating Deepavali in a big way.. But we never failed to light lamps for Vilakkeedu.. There was a firm belief that if you missed one year, you would never be able to keep lighting them again.. Later, with the arrival of Indian television, Deepavali became popular and Vilakkeedu became secondary in many homes, but in our house the custom did not change

There would be a contest between me and my aunt's house over how many lamps to light, who would light first, who would arrange them most beautifully.. In those days, when we proudly showed off all our neatly set lamps together before the wind and drizzle could blow them out, there were no cameras crawling about.. We captured the sights with our eyes..

Amma would carefully put the little clay lamps away to light next year.. Some of the ones put away would have grown mould by the next year… We would push Amma aside, saying all of them would be like that, and buy pretty new lamps.. The grown-up me, raised on the potters' contribution to the economy, stands up for the younger me

Christmas, Vesak: aren't they all festivals of lamps? Perhaps because it has come down as the unbroken witness of human genes from the first humans to today, fire remains to this day an extension of human celebration

When I see the Annamalaiyar lamp, it seems to me that a roaring power is hidden inside that contained flame..

Without measure,

without end,

you create,

you protect,

you destroy:

let the lamps say so
note: Karthigai Vilakkeedu is the Tamil festival of lamps in the month of Karthigai (November–December), especially important in Jaffna; Trisha is a Tamil film actress. Vesak is the Buddhist festival of lights. The Annamalaiyar lamp is the great beacon lit on the hill at Thiruvannamalai for the same festival. The closing words name the three acts of the divine: creation, protection and destruction.
